summary: Tuesday's screened arXiv new-list is strongest on heavy-ion longitudinal structure, low-energy Au+Au proton-flow baselines, and analysis-grade AI/ML methods. The most relevant heavy-ion work concerns d+Au longitudinal entropy deposition, a hadronic EOS baseline for 2.4-4.5 GeV Au+Au flow, STAR fixed-target light-hadron spectra, temperature-fluctuation cumulants, and heavy-flavor radial flow. The strongest transferable AI/ML work covers predictive scaling laws for collider foundation models, neural control variates for LO/NLO event generation, symbolic regression for interpretable TMD extraction, and neural operators/PINN evaluation with realistic caveats.
strongest_paper: 2607.24153: Study the Longitudinal Entropy Deposition using d+Au Collision
top_takeaway: The best heavy-ion paper provides a concrete longitudinal-initial-condition improvement for asymmetric collisions and validates it across several systems. The best AI/ML paper makes collider foundation-model scaling predictive rather than retrospective, with direct planning value for expensive jet-pretraining campaigns.

papers.title: Study the Longitudinal Entropy Deposition using d+Au Collision
papers.authors_short: Zhu Meng, Weiyao Ke, Long-Gang Pang
papers.abstract: The authors sample deuteron configurations from an ab initio wavefunction and introduce a longitudinal entropy deposition model with a transverse entropy coefficient and binary-collision-dependent rapidity loss. In CLVisc plus SMASH, they reproduce d+Au pseudorapidity distributions, spectra, and flow, and report validation in p+Au, He3+Au, and Au+Au.

papers.title: Proton Collectivity in Au+Au Collisions at sqrt(sNN)=2.4-4.5 GeV from a Unified Purely Hadronic EOS without QCD Phase Transition
papers.authors_short: Gao-Feng Wei, Shuang-Jie Liu, Yu-Liang Zhao, Qi-Jun Zhi, Zhigang Xiao
papers.abstract: A purely hadronic transport model with momentum-dependent mean field and K0=230 MeV reproduces proton directed, sideward, and elliptic flow data up to 4.3 GeV, but fails at 4.5 GeV, which the authors interpret as circumstantial evidence for partonic degrees of freedom.

papers.title: Interaction fingerprints in temperature-fluctuation cumulants from the QCD crossover to nuclear liquid-gas criticality
papers.abstract: The paper calculates temperature-fluctuation cumulants in ideal, excluded-volume, and van der Waals HRG models and links their behavior along freeze-out to thermodynamic structures in the QCD crossover and nuclear liquid-gas regions.

papers.title: Light hadron production measurements with Au+Au Collisions from sqrt(sNN)=3.2--4.5 GeV with STAR
papers.authors_short: Mathias C. Labonte, for the STAR Collaboration
papers.abstract: A STAR SQM proceedings report on fixed-target pi, K, and p spectra at 3.2, 3.5, 3.9, and 4.5 GeV, with blast-wave extraction of kinetic freeze-out temperature and surface velocity.

papers.title: Probing collective behaviour of Heavy Quarks through pT-differential radial flow v0(pT)
papers.authors_short: Salvatore Plumari, Maria Lucia Sambataro, Santosh K. Das, Vincenzo Greco
papers.abstract: A proceedings-level proposal for heavy-flavor pT-differential radial flow v0(pT) as a probe of heavy-quark coupling to the QGP, studied with Langevin dynamics coupled to relativistic Boltzmann transport.

papers.title: Predict before you train: Scaling Laws for particle physics foundation models
papers.authors_short: Jan-Lucas Uslu, Benjamin Nachman, Christopher Re
papers.abstract: The paper fits scaling laws on small collider-jet transformers and predicts the loss of models trained with more than 100 times more compute to within one percent, then connects pretraining loss to downstream tagging performance.

papers.title: Neural Control Variates at LO and NLO
papers.authors_short: Theo Heimel, Tilman Plehn, Rebecca Revelli, Sophia Vent, Ramon Winterhalder
papers.abstract: Signed neural control variates built from two normalizing flows reduce event-weight spread and mitigate negative weights in LO and NLO integration and event generation, with the NLO construction interpreted as a trainable complement to subtraction terms.

papers.title: Symbolic Extraction of Non-Perturbative Transverse-Momentum-Dependent Distributions from Drell-Yan Data
papers.authors_short: Cole Granger, Alessandro Bacchetta, Valerio Bertone, Chiara Bissolotti, Matteo Cerutti, Marco Radici, Simone Rodini, Lorenzo Rossi, Cristiano Fanelli
papers.abstract: A neural-network TMD fit to Drell-Yan cross sections is converted into compact analytical expressions by symbolic regression, achieving chi2/ndf=1.040 over 482 points with nine free numerical constants.

papers.title: Extending Fourier Neural Operators for Modeling Parameterized and Coupled PDEs
papers.authors_short: Cheng Jing, Uvini Balasuriya Mudiyanselage, Abhishek Verma, Kallol Bera, Shahid Rauf, Kookjin Lee
papers.abstract: The paper extends Fourier neural operators with hypernetwork parameter conditioning and designs for coupled systems, with benchmarks including capacitively coupled plasma equations and Gray-Scott dynamics.

papers.title: On the post-hoc Evaluation of PDE Discovery: A Multifaceted Challenge of Scientific Advancement
papers.authors_short: Baptiste Mathevon, Farah Cherfaoui, Amaury Habrard, Marc Sebban
papers.abstract: A taxonomy and discussion of PDE-discovery evaluation metrics, emphasizing predictive accuracy, physical consistency, interpretability, and out-of-distribution generalization.

papers.title: Global Convergence of DGM and PINN Algorithms for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
papers.authors_short: Justin Sirignano, Konstantinos Spiliopoulos, Samuel Cohen
papers.abstract: The authors prove global convergence for DGM/PINN training by gradient descent for a class of semi-linear PDEs nonlinear in the solution and first derivative.

cautions.title: Exploring the Effects of Color Reconnection on Net-Charge Fluctuations in pp Collisions at sqrt(s)=2.76 TeV using PYTHIA Monash
cautions.authors_short: Dibakar Dhar, Tumpa Biswas, Zubayer Ahammed, Prabir Kumar Haldar
cautions.abstract: The paper scans PYTHIA Monash color-reconnection configurations for net-charge fluctuations in pp collisions and compares them to ALICE data, finding that current settings overestimate the fluctuations and that CR induces a fixed-multiplicity shift.
